faqs.question: What can I learn from my customers' WhatsApp conversations?
faqs.answer: A business's WhatsApp history shows the questions customers ask most, grouped by product, the things they ask for that the business does not sell, the objections and reasons people did not buy, their mood and motivation, the hours they message, and the answers staff repeat every day. Each of those maps to a decision about stock, prices, offers, staffing or what to automate first.

faqs.question: How do I analyse WhatsApp chats for customer insights?
faqs.answer: Export the chats, remove phone numbers, decide what counts as one conversation (for example, a new conversation after 24 hours of silence), clean the different export formats, label which senders are staff and which are customers, then count keyword patterns and also read samples by hand. Classify every conversation against one fixed list of reasons, measure a second time with a different method, and compare the two before trusting any number.

faqs.question: How do I export a WhatsApp chat for analysis?
faqs.answer: In WhatsApp, open the individual or group chat, open the menu, choose More and then Export chat, and pick Without media or Include media. WhatsApp produces a text file that you can share by email or another app. It cannot be imported back into WhatsApp, and chats with Advanced chat privacy turned on cannot be exported.

faqs.question: Can a text analysis of WhatsApp chats read voice notes and screenshots?
faqs.answer: No. An analysis that reads only the exported text sees a placeholder where a voice note, photo or screenshot was sent, so any request made inside that media is invisible to it. Voice notes have to be transcribed and images read separately. Until that is done, report the share of conversations that contain media as a known gap rather than ignoring it.

faqs.question: Is it safe to upload WhatsApp chats to an AI tool for analysis?
faqs.answer: Only after you remove what identifies people. Strip phone numbers and names from the export before it goes into any tool, check whether the tool's provider keeps or trains on uploaded data, and keep the raw export somewhere only you control. Customer messages often contain addresses and order details, so treat the file as personal data.

faqs.question: What happens when an AI chatbot gives a wrong answer?
faqs.answer: It depends on how the system around the chatbot is built. A well run assistant answers only from the business's own catalogue and policies, says it will check with the team instead of guessing, and lets staff see every conversation live and take it over in the same WhatsApp thread. The damage from a wrong answer is mostly set by how fast someone sees it and corrects it, and whether the customer has to repeat themselves.

faqs.question: What is a silent failure in an AI chatbot?
faqs.answer: A silent failure is when the customer gets no reply at all, even though the system may have generated one. It is often worse than a wrong answer, because nobody sees an error and the customer simply waits. The fix is monitoring that compares replies generated with replies actually delivered, and alerts someone when they do not match.

faqs.question: Can a person take over a WhatsApp chatbot conversation?
faqs.answer: Yes, if the system is built for it. A good takeover sets a flag on that one conversation so the assistant stops replying, lets a staff member answer in the same WhatsApp thread on the same business number, and hands the conversation back to the assistant when the person is done. The assistant should re-check that flag right before it sends anything, because a takeover can happen while it is still writing.

faqs.question: What is the WhatsApp 24 hour customer service window?
faqs.answer: When a customer messages a business on the WhatsApp Business Platform, a 24 hour customer service window opens, and each new message from the customer resets it. Inside the window the business can send free-form replies. Outside it, the business can only send template messages, which generally need Meta's approval first.

faqs.question: When should an AI chatbot hand a conversation to a person?
faqs.answer: When the customer is angry, asks for a refund, raises a health or legal question, asks the same thing more than once, or asks something the assistant cannot answer from the business's own catalogue and policies. Meta's WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy also requires businesses that automate replies to offer prompt, clear and direct escalation paths to a person.

faqs.question: Should a supermarket take orders on WhatsApp if it already has an app?
faqs.answer: Yes, as a second channel and not as a replacement. A grocery app is the better tool for a loyal customer browsing aisles and comparing products. WhatsApp is the better tool for customers who will never install the app, for people arriving from a social media ad, for quick reorders and for customers who already know what they want and would rather type a list. Run both, send WhatsApp orders into the same order system as app orders, and measure each channel separately.

faqs.question: Can customers see products and prices when ordering groceries on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Yes. The WhatsApp Business Platform supports catalogs connected to the business account, single product messages that show one item with its image, price and description, and multi-product messages that show up to 30 products organised into sections. When ordering is enabled, customers can add several items to a cart inside WhatsApp and submit one order, with up to 99 units of each item.

faqs.question: Do WhatsApp grocery orders need a separate system from app orders?
faqs.answer: They should not. A WhatsApp order should arrive in the same order management or ERP system the app feeds, through an API, so stock, picking and delivery treat it like any other order. Where no internal order system exists, a standalone dashboard can list WhatsApp orders until an integration is built. Two separate order books mean retyping, errors and a channel that staff quietly stop using.

faqs.question: Does a customer need an account to order groceries on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: No. On WhatsApp the customer's phone number identifies them, so there is no sign up, no password and no app download. The business can match that number to an existing loyalty or app account if one exists, and saved addresses and order history can follow the customer across both channels.

faqs.question: How do you upsell groceries on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Let the customer state a goal or a list, then build the basket around it. When someone says they are cooking a dish, match every ingredient to a real product on your shelves, show the options with images and prices, and suggest only the items that complete the meal, such as a sauce, a cheese or a dessert. Mention a live offer when it fits the basket, and point out a free delivery threshold when the basket is close to it. One suggestion at each step, and a no ends it.

faqs.question: What are Click to WhatsApp ads?
faqs.answer: Click to WhatsApp ads are a Meta ad format that opens a WhatsApp chat with the business when the person taps the ad, instead of sending them to a website or an app store. They are created in Meta Ads Manager by choosing messaging apps and WhatsApp as the destination. For a grocer, the ad can promote an offer or a recipe and land the shopper directly in a conversation that can take the order.

faqs.question: Are messages from a Click to WhatsApp ad free?
faqs.answer: Under Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform pricing, if a customer messages you through a Click to WhatsApp ad on the WhatsApp Android or iOS app and you reply within the 24 hour customer service window, your first reply opens a free entry point window that can stay open for up to 7 days, during which marketing, utility, authentication and service messages, templates included, are not charged. Meta Business Agent messages are still charged inside it. Outside that window, replies inside the 24 hour customer service window are free for the first 1,000 per business phone number each month and then charged, while marketing templates you send first are charged per delivered message.

faqs.question: Can a WhatsApp chat show product photos and prices?
faqs.answer: Yes. The WhatsApp Business Platform supports a product catalog connected to the business account, single product messages with an image, price and description, and multi-product messages that show up to 30 products in sections. Customers can add items to a cart inside WhatsApp and send one order.

faqs.question: How much does AI customer service cost per month?
faqs.answer: The advertised plan is usually between 10 and 280 US dollars a month, but that is rarely the bill. On vendor pricing pages checked on 3 October 2026, the AI part is often charged separately, at 0.90 to 1.00 US dollars per automated interaction at Gorgias, 0.99 US dollars per outcome at Intercom, and 1.50 to 2.00 US dollars per extra automated resolution at Zendesk. Seats, contact overages and Meta's WhatsApp message fees come on top. A store automating a few hundred conversations a month should budget for the total of all of those, not for the plan price.

faqs.question: What are the hidden costs of an AI chatbot?
faqs.answer: Six lines that the headline price usually leaves out. Per seat charges for the people who still answer. A per resolution or per AI conversation charge for the automation itself. Overage fees when tickets or monthly active contacts pass the plan limit. Meta's WhatsApp template message fees, plus any per message fee a provider adds, such as Twilio's 0.005 US dollars. Add-ons like integrations or extra numbers. And the staff time needed to build, test and maintain the automation, which no invoice shows.

faqs.question: Are WhatsApp replies to customers free?
faqs.answer: Up to a limit. Since 1 October 2026 Meta charges for ordinary replies inside the customer service window after the first 1,000 per business phone number each month. Marketing, utility and authentication templates are charged from the first send, inside or outside that window, and the rate depends on the recipient's country calling code.

faqs.question: Does Meta charge the same WhatsApp rate in Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Meta's rate card prices by the recipient's country calling code. Its pricing documentation lists Saudi Arabia (966) and the United Arab Emirates (971) as their own markets, while Lebanon (961) falls into a grouping called Rest of Middle East. A brand selling across all three should budget per market rather than use one blended rate.

faqs.question: Is a fixed monthly fee better than per resolution pricing?
faqs.answer: It depends on your volume. Per resolution pricing is cheaper when traffic is low or very uneven, because a quiet month costs little. A fixed fee is cheaper and easier to plan when you are growing, because a busy month does not raise the bill. plumcut charges a one time setup fee and a fixed monthly fee in wide traffic bands with a ceiling, and passes Meta messaging and AI model usage through at cost with no margin.

faqs.question: Is an AI chatbot cheaper than hiring a customer service employee?
faqs.answer: For repetitive questions, almost always, because the comparison is not one salary against one subscription. A week has 168 hours and the labour laws of Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Lebanon all cap a standard working week at 48 hours, so covering every hour takes about three and a half full time people before leave. Each one also carries employer costs such as social insurance and an end of service payment. An AI answers at any hour for a monthly fee. It is not cheaper for judgment work, such as complaints and refunds, which should stay with a person.

faqs.question: How many employees do you need to answer WhatsApp 24 hours a day?
faqs.answer: At least three and a half full time employees, and more in practice. A week is 168 hours and the standard maximum working week is 48 hours in Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Lebanon, so 168 divided by 48 gives 3.5 people just to keep one seat filled. Annual leave, sick days and breaks push the real number higher. Most small brands do not do this, which is why messages sent at night or on weekends wait until the morning.

faqs.question: What does a customer service hire really cost an employer in Saudi Arabia?
faqs.answer: More than the salary. For a Saudi employee the employer pays GOSI contributions for annuities, 9 percent for existing contributors and rising in steps toward 11 percent for new entrants under the new Social Insurance Law, plus 2 percent for occupational hazards and 0.75 percent for SANED unemployment insurance. The Labor Law also requires an end of service award of half a month's wage for each of the first five years, at least 21 days of paid annual leave, and a working week capped at 48 hours.

faqs.question: Can AI completely replace customer service staff?
faqs.answer: No, and it should not try. AI is reliable for questions with one correct answer, such as stock, prices, delivery areas, order status and policies, which make up most of the volume in a typical store. Refunds, exceptions and complaints where the business was at fault need a person with the authority to decide. Meta's WhatsApp messaging policy also requires a prompt, clear and direct way to reach a human when replies are automated. The usual result is a smaller team doing better work, not no team.

faqs.question: How much does plumcut cost compared with hiring?
faqs.answer: plumcut charges a one time setup fee and then a fixed monthly fee set by what the solution does, stepping up in wide traffic bands to a ceiling, with Meta messaging and AI usage billed at cost with no margin. There is no gratuity, social insurance, leave cover or recruitment cost, and it answers at every hour of the week. The exact figure depends on the solution and is quoted on a short call, so compare it against the fully loaded cost of the hires it would replace, not against one salary.

faqs.question: Is customer data safe with an AI chatbot on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: It can be, but safety depends on the chain, not the chatbot. A WhatsApp AI usually passes each message through three parties, Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API, the vendor's own servers, and an AI model provider. Meta states that Cloud API messages are encrypted at rest and kept for a maximum of 30 days. The major AI model APIs from OpenAI, Anthropic and Google say they do not train on API data by default. The weakest link is usually the vendor in the middle, so ask where it stores conversations, for how long, and who can read them.

faqs.question: Does the AI train on my customers' WhatsApp messages?
faqs.answer: Not by default at the major model providers. OpenAI says data sent to its API has not been used to train its models since 1 March 2023 unless the customer opts in. Anthropic says it does not use inputs or outputs from its API to train models by default. Google says paid Gemini API prompts and responses are not used to improve its products. Meta's WhatsApp Business Platform terms also restrict using platform data to train AI models, other than fine tuning a model for the business's exclusive use. Ask your vendor to confirm in writing which provider it uses and whether it opted into anything.

faqs.question: Can WhatsApp chatbot data be stored in Saudi Arabia or the UAE?
faqs.answer: For data at rest on Meta's Cloud API, partly. Meta offers a local storage option that keeps message content at rest in a chosen region after processing. The supported region codes listed in Meta's registration documentation include the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain, but not Saudi Arabia or Lebanon. Messages are still processed in Meta data centers before that. Separately, the vendor's own database and the AI provider may store data elsewhere, so ask each one.

faqs.question: What does Saudi Arabia's PDPL mean for a chatbot?
faqs.answer: Saudi Arabia's Personal Data Protection Law came into force on 14 September 2023, with organisations expected to comply by 14 September 2024, and SDAIA is the competent authority. It applies to processing the data of people in the Kingdom even by parties outside it. Transfers outside the Kingdom are conditioned rather than banned, under a separate SDAIA regulation that relies on an adequacy list or safeguards such as standard contractual clauses. A brand selling in Saudi Arabia should ask its chatbot vendor where data goes and which transfer basis it relies on.

faqs.question: Who owns the conversations a chatbot has with my customers?
faqs.answer: Check the contract, because it varies. Some platforms keep conversation history and analytics inside their product, so leaving means losing it. Ask whether you can export every conversation and contact in a usable format, what happens to your data on the day you cancel, and whether the vendor can use your conversations for anything beyond serving your own customers. plumcut's position is that the conversations, and what they show about your customers, belong to the brand and are not locked into a platform or handed to anyone else.

faqs.question: Can one chatbot answer for several stores or brands at once?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it is built as one engine with separate front doors. The shared engine holds the language skills, the policies common to every store and the connections to stock, orders and couriers. Each store keeps its own WhatsApp number, Instagram account or Facebook Page, its own name and tone, its own catalogue, prices, opening hours and delivery areas. The system knows which store a message belongs to from the number, account or Page it arrived on, so the customer only ever talks to the brand they chose.

faqs.question: How many WhatsApp numbers can one business have on the WhatsApp Business Platform?
faqs.answer: Meta's documentation, checked on 25 September 2026, says a new business portfolio is capped at two registered business phone numbers, and the cap rises automatically to 20 once the business is verified or reaches a messaging limit of 2,000. A portfolio can initially hold up to 20 WhatsApp Business Accounts. Messaging limits are set at the portfolio level and shared by every number in it, so one store's large broadcast can use up capacity the other stores needed that day.

faqs.question: Does a customer who messages two of my stores count as one person?
faqs.answer: Not automatically. Messenger gives each person a Page scoped ID and Instagram gives an Instagram scoped ID, and both are unique to the Page or account being messaged, so the same shopper messaging two of your Instagram accounts arrives as two different IDs. On WhatsApp, Meta's business scoped user IDs, which began appearing in webhooks in April 2026, are unique per business portfolio, so numbers in the same portfolio see the same ID. Linking one person across channels still depends on a phone number or email captured in the conversation or already held in your own systems.

faqs.question: How long do I have to reply on WhatsApp, Instagram and Messenger?
faqs.answer: All three give a 24 hour window after the customer's last message. On Messenger and Instagram, a human agent tag lets a person, not an automated reply, respond within 7 days of the customer's message. On WhatsApp, messages outside the 24 hour window have to use a template Meta has approved. Automated replies should therefore be fast enough that the window is rarely the problem, with a clear handover when a human needs more time.

faqs.question: Should every store share the same WhatsApp number?
faqs.answer: Usually not. A shared number makes every store look like one brand, mixes their promotions and their customer history, and lets one store's complaints or blocks affect the rating of a number the others depend on. Separate numbers per store or brand, connected to one shared engine, keep each identity clean while the logic, the integrations and the reporting stay in one place. One number for several branches of the same brand is a reasonable exception.

faqs.question: Should a holding company use one automation system for all its brands?
faqs.answer: In most cases, yes, for the engine and the data, and no, for the customer facing identity. One system behind every brand avoids paying for the same integrations several times, gives the group one view of customers and conversations, and lets improvements made for one brand reach the others. Each brand should still keep its own WhatsApp number, Instagram account and Facebook Page, its own voice, catalogue, prices and promotions. Letting each brand buy its own tool is faster at first and more expensive and less visible every year after.

faqs.question: How should a group roll out conversation automation across its brands?
faqs.answer: One brand at a time. Start with the brand that has the most conversations and the clearest pain, because a quiet brand produces too little data to judge the result. Agree the measures before launch, such as response time, share of conversations resolved without a person and orders placed in chat. Run it long enough to cover a busy period, then reuse the same engine, integrations and reporting for the next brand, changing only what is specific to it.

faqs.question: Can a customer who opted in to one brand be messaged by another brand in the same group?
faqs.answer: Treat each brand's consent as separate. WhatsApp's Business Messaging Policy requires opt in permission before a business contacts someone and requires every opt out request to be honoured, and it does not say that permission given to one business covers a related one. A customer who agreed to hear from one brand has not agreed to hear from its sister brands. Cross brand offers should go through a brand the customer already opted in to, or wait for a fresh opt in.

faqs.question: Should all of a group's brands sit in one Meta business portfolio?
faqs.answer: It is a trade off, checked against Meta's documentation on 25 September 2026. One portfolio means WhatsApp's business scoped user IDs, which are unique per portfolio, identify the same customer consistently across every brand's number, and it means one verification unlocks up to 20 numbers. It also means every number shares one messaging limit, so a large campaign by one brand uses capacity the others need. Brands that are separate legal entities or that broadcast heavily are candidates for their own portfolio.

faqs.question: Can the same system handle retail customers and wholesale buyers?
faqs.answer: Yes, if it is built with separate rules for each. A wholesale buyer ordering stock over WhatsApp needs their own price list, credit terms, minimum quantities and account history, and should never see retail promotions. A retail customer needs the opposite. The language skills, the order connection and the reporting can be shared. The rules, the catalogue and who handles the handover must not be.

faqs.question: What is the difference between an AI agent that answers and one that takes actions?
faqs.answer: An answering agent produces text from knowledge you supply. An acting agent calls another system and changes something in it, such as creating an order, updating a delivery address, raising a return or writing a lead into a CRM. Reads are easy to demonstrate and safe to get wrong. Writes need permissioned credentials, validated inputs, a confirmation step and a log, which is why many vendors stop at lookups.

faqs.question: Which WhatsApp platforms document their AI agent calling an external API?
faqs.answer: Checked on 19 September 2026 against each vendor's own published pages, these do. respond.io documents a Make HTTP Requests action with a limit of ten per agent. SleekFlow documents custom API integrations enabled per agent under Configuration then Actions. Infobip documents external systems as agent tools and chatbots that call external APIs. Yellow.ai documents workflows that connect backend systems by API. Meta documents custom connectors to your external APIs for Meta Business Agent. Vendor documentation shows a capability exists, not that it will work on your stack without building.

faqs.question: Does Meta's own business agent replace these tools?
faqs.answer: It replaces the answering layer for many businesses. Meta said in June 2026 that more than a million businesses were already using a Business Agent on WhatsApp and Messenger, free to activate, with replies billed since 1 August 2026 at 2 US dollars per million tokens, about 4 to 5 cents per message. It does not replace the work of building connectors to your systems, deciding what the agent may change, or keeping it working. Eligibility is also limited by country and by vertical, with finance, government, health, alcohol, gambling, over the counter drugs and matrimony excluded, and one phone number cannot run two competing messaging products at once.

faqs.question: Which tools show the strongest signals for Arabic speaking markets?
faqs.answer: Unifonic is headquartered in Saudi Arabia and publishes a regional AI and data residency position, including partnerships with HUMAIN and Groq. Yellow.ai documents right to left Arabic support in its v3 chat widget and an established Middle East presence. Wati and SleekFlow published Arabic versions of their own websites when we checked on 11 September 2026. None of that demonstrates that an agent reads Gulf dialect or Arabizi correctly in a real customer message, which only a test with your own inbox will show.

faqs.question: Is a managed service better than a self serve platform for this?
faqs.answer: It depends on who will own the work. Self serve platforms cost less in software and require someone in your team to build the actions, test them and repair them when an API changes. A managed service costs more in fees and removes that dependency. If you have a capable owner in house, buy a platform. If nobody on your team will own it and the work spans conversations, a store, payments and internal handovers, a managed service is usually the cheaper answer once staff time is counted.

faqs.question: Does plumcut publish this comparison?
faqs.answer: Yes. plumcut sells a managed WhatsApp service and has a commercial interest in this topic. This guide compares publicly documented capabilities using each vendor's own pages, checked on 19 September 2026, plus editorial judgment about which buyer each approach fits. It is not a hands on benchmark and it does not claim measured superiority over any named vendor.

faqs.question: Is AI customer service the same thing as operations automation?
faqs.answer: No. Customer service automation produces a reply. Operations automation produces a change in a system: an order created, a record updated, a courier booked, an internal task raised. Most requests need both, and a business that automates only the reply still pays a person to do the second half by hand. The reply is also the part that is commoditising fastest, because Meta now ships a business agent that answers on a brand's own WhatsApp number.

faqs.question: What does it actually mean for an AI agent to take an action?
faqs.answer: It means the agent calls another system and changes something there, rather than only reading from it. Looking up an order status is a read. Creating the order, changing a delivery address, raising a return or writing a qualified lead into a CRM is a write. Writes need credentials with permission to change data, validation of what goes in, a confirmation step with the customer, a record of what changed, and a written list of things the agent may never do on its own.

faqs.question: Why is the internal half of a customer request harder in MENA than in Europe or the US?
faqs.answer: Mostly because the data the internal step needs is shaped differently. Saudi Arabia uses a national short address issued by Saudi Post, four letters followed by four digits, for last mile delivery. Dubai uses Makani, a ten digit code from Dubai Municipality that identifies a building entrance. Lebanon has no unified national addressing at all and couriers navigate by landmark. A capture step that asks for a street line and a postal code produces a failed delivery in all three. Add cash on delivery confirmation where it is still used, and Arabizi input that has to become structured data, and the internal half carries work a global template does not account for.

faqs.question: Should an AI agent be allowed to write to my store or CRM?
faqs.answer: Yes, for the narrow set of writes you have defined, with a confirmation step and a log. The safe pattern is a short list of permitted actions, each with validated inputs, rather than broad access to the API. Keep decisions that cost real money, such as refunds above a threshold, discounts beyond policy, and anything touching a disputed order, behind a human approval that the agent prepares but does not grant.

faqs.question: Is Meta's business agent enough on its own?
faqs.answer: It is enough to answer. Meta said in June 2026 that more than a million businesses were already using a Business Agent on WhatsApp and Messenger, and it is free to activate, but since 1 August 2026 its replies are billed at 2 US dollars per million tokens, about 4 to 5 cents per message. Its developer documentation describes custom connectors to external APIs so an agent can check an order or book an appointment. Someone still has to build those connectors against your systems, decide what the agent may change, and keep it working when your API changes. Eligibility is also restricted by vertical and country, and one phone number cannot run two competing messaging products at once.

faqs.question: What should stay with a person when the rest is automated?
faqs.answer: The decisions, not the typing. Approving money out, accepting an order from a delivery area that has lost you money, releasing a refund on a disputed item, and any exception that has never happened before. Automate the holding, the notification, the preparation of everything needed to decide, and the record of what was decided. Never automate the yes itself.

faqs.question: When should you upsell in a customer conversation?
faqs.answer: At four moments, in descending order of how well they work. When the customer has stated a need but not yet chosen a product, because a recommendation is what they asked for. When they have chosen and confirmed, where a genuinely complementary item is a natural addition. When they raise an objection that a different product actually answers. And after delivery, once the order arrived and the customer is satisfied. The moment that does not work is while the customer is waiting for an answer to something else, because an offer there reads as a business ignoring the question.

faqs.question: What is the difference between upselling and cross-selling?
faqs.answer: Upselling offers a better or larger version of what the customer is already buying, such as a bigger size, a longer warranty or a higher specification. Cross-selling offers a different item that goes with it, such as an accessory, a refill or a matching piece. In a conversation cross-selling usually lands better after the customer has committed, because it adds rather than questions the choice they just made, while upselling works best before the decision is final.

faqs.question: How many upsell offers is too many?
faqs.answer: Shopify's own developer guidance for post-purchase offers is to display a maximum of three consecutive offers. In a live conversation the practical limit is lower, usually one, because a conversation has a person in it and a declined offer repeated is experienced as pressure rather than as a second chance. The rule that holds in both places is that a declined offer ends the sequence.

faqs.question: Does it cost money to upsell a customer on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: It depends on when you send it. An offer made inside a live conversation the customer started falls in the 24 hour customer service window, where non-template service messages are free for the first 1,000 per business phone number each month since 1 October 2026, then charged at the service rate. Reaching back out later, for example a cart reminder or a reorder prompt after the window has closed, is a marketing message that needs opt-in and an approved marketing template, and those are charged per delivered message. The offer during a live conversation is the cheap one, and it is also the one that converts best.

faqs.question: Can AI upsell without annoying customers?
faqs.answer: Yes, on three conditions. It only offers something that genuinely relates to what the customer said they want, it offers once and accepts a no, and it never places an offer in front of an unanswered question or a complaint. The failure mode is not automation, it is offering the same thing to everyone regardless of what they asked for. A conversation contains the customer's stated need in their own words, which is more than a product page ever knows.

faqs.question: Where do most upsell tools place the offer?
faqs.answer: On a page. Product page widgets, cart drawers, checkout extensions and post-purchase pages between order confirmation and the thank you page. Apps such as Rebuy, LimeSpot, ReConvert, Selleasy and Aftersell all operate in those surfaces. That works for storefront traffic and it covers none of the customers who skipped the storefront and asked you directly in a message, which in many regional retail businesses is a large share of the buyers.

faqs.question: How many customer messages a day is too many to handle manually?
faqs.answer: There is no universal number, because the load comes from the shape of the messages rather than the count. A store answering 200 messages a day that are variations of six questions is doing lookup work a machine can do. A store answering 60 messages that are all different is doing real work that needs a person. Count your distinct questions before you count your messages, and measure the share you answer within an hour. When that share falls below roughly half on an ordinary day, manual handling has already stopped working.

faqs.question: Should I hire more staff or automate customer service?
faqs.answer: Hiring adds capacity in a straight line and automation adds it in a step. If your volume is growing, hiring means your cost per order stays flat forever, because every doubling of messages needs another doubling of people. Automation costs more to set up and then absorbs growth without adding headcount. The practical answer for most growing retail shops is both: automate the repeated factual questions, and keep your people for the conversations where judgment and goodwill decide the outcome.

faqs.question: What breaks first when a retail shop gets too busy to answer messages?
faqs.answer: Speed goes first, then consistency, then coverage outside working hours, then the ability to read your own messages at all. Revenue damage starts at the second stage, when different staff give different answers to the same question, and gets worse at the third, when evening and weekend buyers go unanswered. The fourth failure is the one nobody notices, because losing the record of what customers keep asking for has no visible symptom.

faqs.question: Does automating customer service cost more as my store grows?
faqs.answer: It depends on the billing unit, and the difference is large at volume. Tools that bill per resolved conversation or per monthly active contact cost more as you grow, because both meters read your growth back to you as cost. A fixed monthly fee set by what the system does rather than by how busy it gets does not move with a busy month. Compare vendors on the unit first and the price second, and project both at three times your current volume.

faqs.question: Do I need the WhatsApp Business API to handle high message volume?
faqs.answer: The free WhatsApp Business app has no way to connect your store data, no reliable multi person access and no automation beyond simple canned replies, so it stops working as a system somewhere in the low hundreds of messages a day. The WhatsApp Business Platform is what allows order lookups, stock checks and automated answers grounded in real data. Replying to customers who messaged you first is not what costs money on that platform, because service messages sent inside the 24 hour customer service window are not charged.

faqs.question: Can AI handle retail customer service?
faqs.answer: Yes for questions that have exactly one correct answer, which in most retail stores is the majority of incoming volume. Stock, price, delivery timelines, payment methods, store hours, return policy and order status are all deterministic, meaning the right answer comes from a written policy or from live store data rather than from judgment. It should not handle refunds, goodwill decisions, complaints where the business is at fault, price negotiation or wholesale enquiries, because the correct answer there depends on what the business is willing to do for that specific customer.

faqs.question: How much does AI customer service cost for a retail store?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the billing unit, and vendors use at least five different ones. Per resolved conversation, roughly 0.90 to 1.50 US dollars at Gorgias, Intercom and Zendesk as listed on their pricing pages in September 2026. Per AI conversation at Tidio. Per monthly active contact at respond.io, Wati and Manychat. Per seat at Intercom. Or a fixed monthly fee that does not move with volume, which is how plumcut prices. Compare the unit before the number, because the unit decides what happens to your bill when your traffic doubles.

faqs.question: What is a resolution in AI customer service pricing?
faqs.answer: A resolution is a customer conversation the automation closed without a human stepping in. Intercom counts it when the customer either confirms the answer was satisfactory or leaves without asking for more help. Zendesk counts a request resolved by automation with no escalation to a human. Gorgias bills per resolved interaction. The practical consequence is that you are billed for closed support conversations, so the metric counts deflected work and never counts a sale.

faqs.question: Does AI customer service integrate with my online store?
faqs.answer: Most tools integrate with Shopify, WooCommerce and BigCommerce, because that is where their customers are. Coverage for the Gulf store platforms is much thinner. Salla and Zid both publish merchant APIs and support WhatsApp integration through their own app stores, but neither appeared on the Gorgias, Zendesk, Intercom, Siena or Tidio integration listings checked on 13 September 2026, so a store on either one usually needs a custom connection rather than an off the shelf app.

faqs.question: Will AI customer service lose my customers?
faqs.answer: Only if you trap them. Automated service fails at the handover rather than at the answer. Customers accept a fast machine answer to a factual question and reject being stuck with one when their question has feeling in it. Meta's WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy permits automation inside the 24 hour customer service window and requires prompt, clear and direct escalation paths in the same breath, so a visible route to a person is both the better experience and a policy requirement.

faqs.question: Is AI customer service worth it for a small retail shop?
faqs.answer: Not always. The trigger is repetition rather than size. If the same handful of questions arrives often enough that answering them is a job, and late enough that answering them costs sales, automation removes real work. If your questions are all different, or you are still agreeing internally on what the answers are, automation has nothing to remove and adds a system to maintain.

faqs.question: How many messages a day do you need before automating is worth it?
faqs.answer: There is no universal number, because the cost is in the questions rather than the messages. A store answering forty messages a day that are all variations of three questions has more to gain than one answering a hundred messages that are all different. Count your repeated questions before you count your messages.

faqs.question: Does it cost more to reply to customers on WhatsApp once you automate?
faqs.answer: Only a little for replies. Meta made service conversations free on 1 November 2024, but since 1 October 2026 it charges for non-template service replies inside an open customer service window after the first 1,000 per business phone number each month. Template messages are charged per delivered message.

faqs.question: Is my business too small for AI customer service?
faqs.answer: If you are pre-launch, selling to friends, or taking orders by phone, then yes, and the honest advice is to wait. Automation removes repetition. Before you have repetition, it removes nothing and adds a system to maintain.

faqs.question: What should I do instead if I am not ready yet?
faqs.answer: Write down every question a customer asks you for two weeks. That list is the only real input an automation needs, it costs nothing to build, and it stays useful whether you automate in three months or never.

faqs.question: Is WhatsApp cheaper than SMS for delivery notifications?
faqs.answer: Usually, but not because the unit price is lower. Both charge you for the message you send first. The difference is everything after it. SMS bills every message including the ones you send to answer a question, while on WhatsApp a customer's reply opens a 24 hour customer service window, and since 1 October 2026 service messages inside it are free for the first 1,000 per business phone number each month, then charged at the service rate. If your dispatch notification produces conversations, WhatsApp bills the notification and usually little else, while SMS bills the whole exchange. If it produces nothing but silence, the two are close and you should compare the current rate cards for your market.

faqs.question: Can a customer reply to an SMS delivery notification?
faqs.answer: Not when it comes from an alphanumeric sender name, which is how most branded notification SMS is sent in this region. Alphanumeric sender IDs are one way by design and recipients cannot reply to them. Providers note that because customers cannot even send STOP, you have to give them another way to opt out. If you want replies you need a real number, which is a separate registration with its own rules per country.

faqs.question: What does it take to start sending notification SMS in the UAE or Saudi Arabia?
faqs.answer: A registered sender ID, and it is paperwork rather than code. UAE operators require registration documents that depend on where your company is based and where the traffic originates, and the UAE regulator applied new fees for international alphanumeric sender IDs from 1 January 2025, which providers pass on. Twilio, for example, lists a one time setup fee of 225 dollars per international sender ID and 115 dollars per month to keep it. Saudi Arabia has its own registration, and Mobily stopped supporting promotional sender ID registration in April 2024.

faqs.question: Do I need customer opt in for WhatsApp delivery updates?
faqs.answer: Yes. Meta's business messaging policy requires an opt in before you message someone, it has to name your business, and it can be collected outside WhatsApp as long as you follow local law. You also cannot open the conversation with free text: a business initiated message has to use a template approved in advance, categorised by what it does, with delivery updates falling under utility.

faqs.question: When is SMS still the right channel for an order update?
faqs.answer: When the message has to arrive whether or not the person uses WhatsApp, when it needs no reply, and when a data connection cannot be assumed. One time passwords, a hard cutoff notice, and the fallback for a customer whose WhatsApp template did not get delivered are all good SMS. Most stores end up running both rather than choosing, with WhatsApp as the default and SMS behind it.

faqs.question: Does a delivered notification mean the parcel arrived?
faqs.answer: No, on either channel. A delivery receipt describes your message, not your shipment. Track parcel state from your courier's data and message state from your messaging provider, and never let one stand in for the other in a customer facing reply.

faqs.question: What is manual order entry in delivery software?
faqs.answer: It is a person reading an order from somewhere else, usually a WhatsApp thread, a phone call or an email, and typing it into the delivery or fleet platform as a new job. The order already exists as a decision between you and the customer. Manual entry is the step that turns it into a row the system can dispatch, and it is pure re-keying, because no new information is created by the typing.

faqs.question: Is automated order capture more accurate than a person typing?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and the honest answer is that it moves the errors rather than removing them. A person mis-hears a street name; an automated capture accepts an address the customer wrote badly. The real gain is that validation runs on every order instead of on the ones an agent happens to double check, and the rules are written once rather than living in one experienced person's head. An automated capture with no validation layer is worse than a careful agent.

faqs.question: Do I need to replace my delivery software to automate order entry?
faqs.answer: No, in most cases. Established delivery and fleet platforms expose a REST API for creating jobs and webhooks for status changes, which is the same route their own integrations use. If your platform has that, the conversational layer sits in front of it and writes into the system you already run. If it has no API at all, that is a real blocker and worth asking your vendor about before changing anything else.

faqs.question: When is manual order entry still the right choice?
faqs.answer: When volume is low enough that the typing costs less than the integration, when nearly every order is negotiated rather than repeated, or when your platform genuinely has no API. A few orders a day handled by someone who knows the customers does not need automating. The case changes when the same order shape is being retyped dozens of times a day and mistakes start costing you failed deliveries.

faqs.question: What happens to orders the automation cannot handle?
faqs.answer: They should go to a person, with the conversation attached, and that path is not a failure of the design. A good capture flow decides between a complete order it can create, an incomplete one it should ask about, and an unusual one it should hand over. The number worth watching is how often handover happens and why, because that list tells you what to fix next.

faqs.question: What does it take to create an order in fleet software from a WhatsApp message?
faqs.answer: Four things. A WhatsApp Business API number so a system can receive and send messages, a layer that reads the conversation and extracts the order fields, a validation step that refuses to create an order it cannot dispatch, and an authenticated call to your platform's create job endpoint carrying your own reference so the order cannot be duplicated. The platform's status webhooks then close the loop by pushing updates back into the same thread.

faqs.question: Can this work if my logistics platform is custom built rather than off the shelf?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is often easier. A custom platform means the team that owns the database can add a create order endpoint and a status webhook shaped exactly the way the conversation layer needs them, instead of you working around a vendor's field names. What matters is that something authenticated exists to write an order and something exists to tell you when its status changes.

faqs.question: Should a logistics software company build conversational ordering itself or partner?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether conversation is your product. Message handling is not a feature you ship once. It is a live surface with template approvals, a 24 hour reply window, per market pricing, and language behaviour that has to survive real customers writing badly. If your roadmap is routing, dispatch and proof of delivery, the honest comparison is between a partner who maintains that surface and the engineering months you would spend maintaining it yourself.

faqs.question: What stops a duplicate order being created when a customer repeats themselves?
faqs.answer: An idempotency reference generated from the conversation and sent with the create call, so a second attempt with the same reference updates rather than creates. Delivery platforms generally let you attach your own external identifier to a job for exactly this purpose. Without it, a customer who says "yes, confirm" twice produces two dispatches, and that is the most common way an integration like this loses money.

faqs.question: Does the customer have to leave WhatsApp at any point?
faqs.answer: No, that is the point of doing it this way. The order is captured in the thread, the order number is returned into the same thread, and status changes arrive there too. Sending the customer to a portal or a form reintroduces exactly the step that made people reply in the chat in the first place.

faqs.question: How are order notifications billed on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: A message you send first, outside an open customer service window, is a template message billed at the rate for that customer's market, while replies inside the 24 hour window the customer opened are free for the first 1,000 per business phone number each month, then charged. Rates are market specific and Meta has revised its rate card, so check the current card rather than a figure quoted in an article. We covered the detail in our piece on what the WhatsApp Business API really costs.

faqs.question: What should a small online store automate first?
faqs.answer: The repeated questions that have exactly one correct answer: opening hours, delivery zones and times, sizing guidance, returns policy and payment methods. They need no integration, no approved template and little in message fees, because replies sent inside the 24 hour customer service window a customer opens are free for the first 1,000 per business phone number each month. Writing those answers down properly is also the specification for every later stage.

faqs.question: Do I need the WhatsApp Business API to start automating?
faqs.answer: Not for the first stage. Fixed answers to inbound questions can start on the free WhatsApp Business app with its built in away messages and quick replies. You need the WhatsApp Business Platform once you want replies that read live data from your store, or once you want to message a customer first outside the 24 hour window, which requires an approved template.

faqs.question: How do I know if a task is worth automating?
faqs.answer: Score it on two axes: how often it happens, and whether a competent new hire with your policy document and read access to your store could get it right every time without asking anyone. High frequency plus one correct answer is worth automating now. Low frequency plus a judgment call is worth leaving with a person indefinitely.

faqs.question: What should never be automated in a store?
faqs.answer: Refunds and goodwill decisions, complaints where your business is at fault, price negotiation, and wholesale or partnership enquiries. These are commercial judgments about a specific relationship. Meta's Business Messaging Policy also requires that automated responses come with prompt, clear and direct escalation paths, so a route to a person is a policy requirement, not an optional extra.

faqs.question: How long does each stage take to set up?
faqs.answer: Stage one is limited by how fast you can write your policies down, usually days rather than weeks. Stage two depends on your store data being clean, particularly whether the phone number on an order matches the number the customer messages from. Stage three is gated by Meta's template review, which is a queue outside your control, so plan around it rather than against it.

faqs.question: Should I automate marketing messages early?
faqs.answer: No. Marketing templates require opt in, cost the marketing rate, and generate blocks faster than any other category when they are sent to people who did not expect them. Blocks lower your quality rating, and a lowered quality rating reduces the number of people you are permitted to message at all. Earn the reactive stages first.

faqs.question: Does WhatsApp automation actually increase sales?
faqs.answer: It can, through three mechanisms: answering buying questions while the customer is still deciding, covering the hours your team does not work, and following up on unfinished orders systematically. The size depends on your conversation volume, your current conversion rate, your average order value and your margin, not on the software. If you already reply within minutes at every hour, two of the three mechanisms are already spent.

faqs.question: How do I calculate whether automation would pay for itself?
faqs.answer: Work out how many additional orders a month would cover the cost at your gross margin, then express that as the change in conversion rate it implies across your current volume of buying conversations. If the required change is a couple of percentage points and you know you lose more than that to slow replies, the case is strong. If it requires conversion to double, it is not.

faqs.question: Why should I distrust vendor ROI figures?
faqs.answer: Because an uplift figure needs a baseline, a period, a population and a control to mean anything, and vendor case studies rarely publish any of them. A store that grew after installing a tool usually also entered a season, ran ads and changed something else. plumcut sells in this category and publishes about it, which is why this article gives you a model instead of a number.

faqs.question: Which parts of conversation automation cost money?
faqs.answer: Only the messages you send first. Since 1 October 2026, service messages inside the 24 hour customer service window are free for the first 1,000 per business phone number each month and then charged at the service rate, so faster replies cost little or nothing per message. Cart reminders and other outbound follow up are marketing templates, which need opt in and are billed at the marketing rate for that market.

faqs.question: How do I measure recovered orders honestly?
faqs.answer: With a holdout. Randomly withhold follow up from a share of eligible customers and compare the two groups. Without one you are counting people who would have returned anyway, which is the most common reason recovery figures are overstated. Compare against the holdout rather than against last month, because seasonality and advertising will swamp the effect you are looking for.

faqs.question: When is conversation automation not worth buying?
faqs.answer: When your buying conversation volume is low enough that a person can genuinely answer all of them, when each sale is a high value negotiated relationship where speed is not the constraint, or when your stock and price data is not reliable enough to quote. In the last case automation will confidently sell things you cannot ship, which is worse than doing nothing.

faqs.question: Can I get courier tracking data automatically?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, through the carrier's API. Aramex, for example, publishes a shipments tracking API in its developer solutions centre that accepts a list of waybill numbers and returns their tracking data, requiring a registered account with credentials. Access is typically pull based rather than pushed to you, so how fresh your data is depends on how often you poll, and carriers differ in what they expose.

faqs.question: Does a delivered status on WhatsApp mean the parcel arrived?
faqs.answer: No. Meta's status webhook describes your message, not your shipment. Delivered means the message reached at least one of the customer's devices. A message can stay at sent because the customer has not come online, and Meta holds messages for offline customers for a 30 day window. Track parcel state and message state as two separate things.

faqs.question: Should I send an out for delivery message?
faqs.answer: Only if your courier updates that status early enough on the delivery day to be useful. A notification that arrives after the parcel has already been delivered is a paid message that makes your business look disorganised. If the carrier's timing is unreliable, send the dispatch notification and skip this one.

faqs.question: How should automation handle a failed delivery attempt?
faqs.answer: By escalating, not by messaging alone. Map the failure status to an internal alert with a named owner and a deadline measured in hours, because whether a reattempt is worth a second leg is a commercial decision, particularly on cash on delivery. Contact the customer with a concrete next option rather than an apology, and log the reason in a fixed vocabulary so the pattern behind repeated failures becomes visible.

faqs.question: Do delivery notifications cost money?
faqs.answer: A notification you send first, when no customer service window is open, is a utility template and is billed at the rate for that customer's market. Since 1 October 2026, replies inside the 24 hour window a customer opened are free for the first 1,000 per business phone number each month, then charged, and utility templates are charged even when sent in response to a user. Meta revised its rate cards effective 1 July 2026 and rates are market specific, so check the current card rather than a quoted figure.

faqs.question: What changes when orders are cash on delivery?
faqs.answer: The delivery attempt is also the payment attempt, so a failed attempt is a cancelled sale plus two legs of shipping rather than a rescheduling. Confirm the order and the delivery window before dispatch instead of after, state the amount and the currency the customer will be asked for, and give them a way to change the day before the driver leaves.

faqs.question: What internal work should a small store automate first?
faqs.answer: The order handover: the moment an agreed order becomes a record in your store, a shipment with a courier, a task for whoever packs, and a line in your weekly view. It is the highest frequency retype in a commerce business and the one where a dropped digit costs a real delivery. Keep the decision to accept, prioritise or hold an order with a person.

faqs.question: Can I automate internal operations without buying new software?
faqs.answer: Often yes. Shopify Flow can trigger on store events, filter on conditions about the order or customer, and then add order tags, hold a fulfillment order, send an email, send a Slack message or send an HTTP request to an external service. WooCommerce emits webhooks on topics such as order.created and order.updated with a signed payload. Most small team handovers fit inside those primitives.

faqs.question: How do I know a task is worth automating internally?
faqs.answer: Ask whether a person is moving information that already exists without changing it, or weighing information and choosing. The first is a retype and should always be automated. The second is a decision and should stay with a person, with the information reaching them faster instead. Below roughly weekly frequency, doing it by hand is usually still the right answer.

faqs.question: Should staff questions and customer questions use the same system?
faqs.answer: The same written answers, in separate spaces, with an explicit boundary. Internal answers include margins, supplier names and policy limits that must never be reachable from a customer facing channel. Build the customer facing set first, because it pays back sooner, then extend it internally.

faqs.question: What should we still approve manually?
faqs.answer: A short list where a mistake costs real money: discounts past a threshold, refunds over an amount, orders to delivery areas that have lost you money, and first orders from new wholesale accounts. Automate the holding, the notification and the record of what was decided. Never automate the yes itself.

faqs.question: Why does internal automation fail in small teams?
faqs.answer: Usually because the process was never agreed. If two people perform the same handover differently, automating it encodes the disagreement instead of resolving it. The other common cause is silent failure: a webhook stops firing and nobody notices for a week, which is worse than a manual step somebody owns.

faqs.question: Does Meta allow automated replies on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Yes. The WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy permits businesses to use automation when responding during the 24 hour customer service window, but requires that prompt, clear and direct escalation paths are also available. Businesses must also honour requests to opt out or discontinue messages. Automation with no route to a person is a policy problem as well as a service problem.

faqs.question: What should never be handled by automated customer service?
faqs.answer: Refunds, exchanges and goodwill decisions, complaints where your business is at fault, price negotiation, wholesale and partnership enquiries, and anything legal, medical or safety related. The test is not difficulty but whether the correct response depends on who this specific customer is and what you are willing to do for them.

faqs.question: Does automating support cost money per message?
faqs.answer: Only a little for replies to customers. Service messages are the replies you send inside the 24 hour customer service window that a customer's message opens, and since 1 October 2026 Meta charges for them only after the first 1,000 per business phone number each month. What costs money is messaging a customer first outside that window, which requires an approved template.

faqs.question: How do I stop an AI giving customers wrong information?
faqs.answer: Ground it and let it refuse. Only automate answers that are deterministic, either from a written policy or from live store data, and write explicit refusal sentences for everything else. A fluent, confident, wrong answer about stock or price costs more than no answer, because it produces an order you cannot fill and a customer who stops trusting anything you say.

faqs.question: What happens if customers block or report my business?
faqs.answer: Blocks and reports feed your number's quality rating, and Meta reduces a number's messaging limit by one level immediately if its quality rating has been Flagged for seven days. The messaging limit caps how many unique people you can message outside a customer service window in a moving 24 hour period. Excessive negative feedback can lead to a business being limited or offboarded, so poor automated service directly reduces how many customers you may reach.

faqs.question: Will customers notice they are talking to automation?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and that is fine. What damages the relationship is not being automated, it is being trapped, being told something untrue, or having to repeat yourself to the human who takes over. A system that answers instantly, says clearly what it cannot do, and hands over with the full context intact reads as competence rather than as a wall.

faqs.question: Does answering "where is my order" on WhatsApp cost anything?
faqs.answer: Not much when you are replying. A customer message opens a 24 hour customer service window, and since 1 October 2026 Meta charges for service messages sent inside it only after the first 1,000 per business phone number each month. What costs money is messaging first, for example a dispatch notification sent when no window is open, which is billed as a utility template at the rate for that customer's country.

faqs.question: Can I send tracking updates before the customer asks?
faqs.answer: Yes, with an approved utility template and the customer's opt in. Sent outside an open customer service window it is charged at the utility rate. Sent inside one it is also charged at the utility rate, since 1 October 2026. Most brands find that one dispatch notification per order pays for itself by removing the question entirely.

faqs.question: What happens when one order ships in two boxes?
faqs.answer: A Shopify fulfilment carries a single tracking number, so a split shipment is two fulfilments and two events, while your customer is still thinking about one order. Decide the wording in advance. Say which items have shipped and which are still coming, because a plain "your order is on its way" gets discovered at the door.

faqs.question: Do I need the WhatsApp Business API to automate order status?
faqs.answer: For reactive answers to customers who message you, not necessarily. For proactive updates you send first, yes. The free WhatsApp Business app cannot send a template to a customer outside the 24 hour window and cannot read your store data, so anything that fires automatically on a fulfilment event needs the WhatsApp Business Platform.

faqs.question: How quickly does an order status reply need to arrive?
faqs.answer: Fast enough to land while the customer is still in the app, which in practice means seconds rather than minutes. Speed also keeps the reply cheap, since it happens inside the customer service window the customer just opened, where the first 1,000 service replies per number each month are free. A reply that arrives the next morning costs you the same as no reply.

faqs.question: Is the WhatsApp Business API free?
faqs.answer: Separate Meta messaging charges from the rest of the setup. Some messages have no Meta charge under the free messaging rules, but a provider, software platform or implementation partner may still charge for its service. Free messaging is not the same as free operation.

faqs.question: What is the 24 hour customer service window?
faqs.answer: A customer message opens or resets a 24 hour customer service window, and inside it a business can reply without a template. Since 1 October 2026 Meta charges for those service replies again, after a free tier of 1,000 service messages per business phone number each month, and utility templates sent inside an open window are charged too. Provider charges need to be assessed separately.

faqs.question: Are volume discounts a free tier?
faqs.answer: No. Utility and authentication volume tiers can reduce eligible message rates. A discounted message can still have a charge. Calculate the applicable tiers and market rates instead of counting discounted traffic as free.

faqs.question: Does Lebanon have its own WhatsApp message rate?
faqs.answer: No. As of 1 October 2026, Meta's rate card prices Lebanon under the "Rest of Middle East" region, together with Bahrain, Jordan and Yemen, at 0.0392 US dollars per marketing message and 0.0091 per utility or authentication message. Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Egypt and Iraq are each priced as standalone markets. Because Meta charges by the recipient's country calling code rather than your business location, a Lebanese brand selling into Saudi Arabia is billed at the Saudi rate.

faqs.question: What should I ask a vendor to include in a quote?
faqs.answer: Ask for Meta charges, provider fees, software or AI allowances, one-time setup, maintenance, support, and overage terms. Give vendors the same workload and required integrations so you can compare equivalent scopes.

faqs.question: Does WhatsApp automation work with Shopify?
faqs.answer: Yes. Shopify exposes products, inventory, orders and fulfilment through its API, so an automation layer can check real stock, show a real product and return a real order status. The quality of the setup depends far more on how clean your catalogue is than on the integration itself.

faqs.question: Will it understand Arabic and Arabizi?
faqs.answer: A modern language model handles Arabic, English and the Latin-script Arabizi that Gulf and Lebanese shoppers actually type, including the number substitutions like 3 for ain and 7 for haa. Keyword and menu based bots do not, because the same word gets spelled six different ways.

faqs.question: Can it take payment inside the chat?
faqs.answer: It depends on your market and payment provider. In much of the region cash on delivery is still dominant, so a good setup confirms the order in chat and hands off to your existing fulfilment rather than forcing a card payment the customer did not want.

faqs.question: What about customers who want a human?
faqs.answer: They get one. Every setup needs a clean handover to a person, and the customer should be able to trigger it at any time. An automation that traps someone is worse than no automation, because it costs you the sale and the trust at the same time.

faqs.question: How long does setup take for a Shopify store?
faqs.answer: Two to four weeks in practice. The connection is quick. What takes the time is auditing the catalogue, writing down the policies your team knows but has never documented, getting templates approved, and testing what happens when the AI does not know something.

faqs.question: Is an abandoned cart message marketing or utility on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Marketing. Meta's template categorization documentation lists cart abandonment reminders under Marketing examples, alongside promotions and retargeting. Utility is for following up on a user action, such as an order or delivery update. Filing a cart reminder as utility is a misclassification, not a cost saving, and category is reviewed rather than taken on trust.

faqs.question: Do I need opt in to send a cart reminder?
faqs.answer: Yes. Meta requires opt in before you message anyone on WhatsApp. It does not have to be WhatsApp specific, a general marketing consent is acceptable where local law allows, but it must clearly name your business so the person knows who they agreed to hear from. Having their number from a past order is not opt in.

faqs.question: Can I use the same opt in for order updates and marketing?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most common mistake. They are separate permissions. Someone consenting to delivery updates has not consented to promotional messages, and treating one as the other is what generates blocks and reports. Use two checkboxes at checkout.

faqs.question: How many reminders can I send?
faqs.answer: Meta does not publish a number, but the practical answer is one. Repeatedly messaging someone who has not replied is what gets you blocked, and blocks lower your quality rating, which in turn limits how many messages you are allowed to send at all. The cost of over sending is not the message fee, it is your capacity.

faqs.question: Is there a cheaper way to recover carts on WhatsApp?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is not misclassifying templates. Since 1 October 2026, replies inside the 24 hour customer service window are free for the first 1,000 per business phone number each month, then charged at the service rate, and a customer arriving from a click to WhatsApp ad on the WhatsApp Android or iOS app can open a free entry point window that can stay open for up to 7 days from your first reply, though Meta Business Agent messages are still charged inside it. Conversations you are invited into cost little or nothing; conversations you start cost the marketing rate. Design for the first.

faqs.question: Does a discount have to be in the message?
faqs.answer: No, and adding one does not change the category. A reminder is marketing either way, because the objective is commercial. Whether a discount improves recovery is a margin question for your business, not a compliance or pricing one.

faqs.question: Is a shared inbox limited to rule based automation?
faqs.answer: No. A shared inbox describes how a team manages conversations, not the intelligence of its automation. Some platforms also offer AI replies and actions. Check the features in the specific plan and test them with your own catalogue and customer questions before deciding.

faqs.question: Which WhatsApp tool is cheapest?
faqs.answer: There is no universal cheapest option. Compare Meta charges, provider fees, software subscriptions, AI usage, setup work and ongoing staff time for the same workload. An API service can suit a developer team, while a platform or managed service can reduce the work your team must perform.

faqs.question: Can I use the WhatsApp Business app?
faqs.answer: It can be a useful starting point when a person can keep up with conversations using greetings, away messages and saved replies. Decide from missed messages, workload and integration needs, rather than a universal messages-per-day threshold.

faqs.question: Which WhatsApp automation tools are compared here?
faqs.answer: Twilio and 360dialog as API and infrastructure options, Gupshup as an enterprise leaning stack, Wati, Interakt, respond.io and SleekFlow as self serve platforms, Zoko as a Shopify focused platform with outcome based AI pricing, and plumcut as a managed service. Each entry links to the vendor's own public pricing page, read on 11 September 2026.

faqs.question: Which WhatsApp platforms offer an Arabic interface?
faqs.answer: Of the tools we checked on 11 September 2026, Wati and SleekFlow publish Arabic language versions of their own websites. That signals regional intent but does not demonstrate that the agent reads Gulf dialect or Arabizi correctly in a customer message. Test dialect and Arabizi handling yourself with real messages from your inbox before committing.

faqs.question: Can AI actually understand Gulf and Levantine dialects, or only Modern Standard Arabic?
faqs.answer: Modern systems handle dialect far better than they did, but capability varies a lot by vendor and by dialect, and no vendor's marketing page will tell you where its limits are. The only reliable answer comes from testing with your own customers' messages, in dialect and Arabizi, with the typos left in. Twenty real messages will tell you more than any demo.

faqs.question: Do I need separate WhatsApp templates for Arabic and English?
faqs.answer: Yes. Meta requires you to assign a language code when creating a template and does not translate template strings or variables for you, so each language is a separate template you submit and get approved. You can give templates in different languages the same name, which keeps them organised, but each one goes through review independently and can be approved or rejected on its own.

faqs.question: What is Arabizi and does it matter for customer service?
faqs.answer: Arabizi is Arabic written in Latin characters, using numerals for sounds with no Latin equivalent, as in "3andkon" or "kifak". It is extremely common in messaging across the Levant and the Gulf, particularly among younger customers. It matters because systems that only parse Arabic script or English words treat it as noise, which means a real share of your inbound messages get misunderstood.

faqs.question: Should our automated messages use dialect or Modern Standard Arabic?
faqs.answer: For templates you send first, plain Modern Standard Arabic is the safer default, because it is understood across every market and does not sound out of place in any of them. Dialect is warmer but localises you, so Levantine phrasing reads as foreign in the Gulf. In live conversation, matching how the customer writes is better than either default.

faqs.question: Does replying in Arabic cost more than replying in English?
faqs.answer: No. Meta's rates depend on the template category and the recipient's country calling code, not on the language of the message. What does change your costs is where your customers are, since a campaign spanning Saudi Arabia, the UAE and Lebanon crosses several rate cards. Replies inside the 24 hour customer service window are a different matter and are not template sends.

faqs.question: Can I automate WhatsApp for free?
faqs.answer: Partly. The free WhatsApp Business app offers greetings, away messages and saved replies for a person to use. More integrated automation can use the Cloud API. Meta charges for delivered template messages and, since 1 October 2026, for service replies beyond 1,000 free per business phone number each month; your software or provider may charge separately.

faqs.question: Will automating WhatsApp get my number banned?
faqs.answer: Official tools do not guarantee that an account will never be restricted. Your messaging must still follow Meta's policies, including consent and applicable content rules. Check the current WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy before launching outbound campaigns and monitor account quality after launch.

faqs.question: Does WhatsApp automation work in Arabic?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Cloud API is language agnostic, and modern language models handle Arabic, English and the mixed Arabizi that MENA shoppers actually type. What breaks is usually the product catalogue and the policy text behind the bot, not the language itself. plum is built for Arabic and English side by side.

faqs.question: How long does it take to set up?
faqs.answer: The free Business app takes an afternoon. A working Cloud API setup with a real catalogue, order lookups and a tested handover to a human is closer to two to four weeks, most of which is writing down what your team already knows. See how we run that in our build process.
